docs.title: Cobblemon PokeTowns
docs.text:
Not released yet

PokeTowns has no public download yet. These pages describe the current development build, 0.0.11, and only what that build does. Anything not described here is not in the mod yet.

docs.title: Cobblemon PokeTowns
docs.text:
Pokémon-themed settlements for your Cobblemon world. Villages and Towns grow around a Pokémon Center in the plaza, Towns add a Poké Mart across the square, and some Towns have a gym behind the Center. They take the place of vanilla villages, and one switch brings vanilla villages back.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge

Get started Settlements

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 🏘️ Villages and Towns generate through Minecraft's own structure system, in the same biomes as vanilla villages, with streets, houses, farms and villagers.
  • 🏥 A Pokémon Center in every plaza heals your team for free, with a PC, a waystone and Nurse Joy behind the counter.
  • 🛒 The Poké Mart stands across the plaza in every Town.
  • 🥇 Gyms: three Towns in ten have one, and with the COBBLEVERSE datapack it is one of its Kanto gyms with the leader inside.
  • 🧩 Configurable: keep or bring back vanilla villages, and choose how far apart settlements are when you create the world.
  • 🛣️ Works with Routes: Routes finds every PokeTowns settlement as a village and connects it to the road network.

💛 Enjoying the mod?

PokeTowns is made by shiero in their free time. If it made your world more fun, consider sponsoring shiero.

License

PokeTowns is source-available with revenue share: free for personal and non-commercial use with attribution; any revenue-generating use requires sharing revenue with the author. In short: if you make money, shiero makes money.

docs.title: Pokémon Center & Poké Mart
docs.text: Every settlement has a Pokémon Center in its plaza. Every Town also has a Poké Mart across the square.

docs.title: The Pokémon Center
docs.text:
What How it works Healing machines heal your team for free, as Cobblemon's healing machine always does PC Cobblemon's PC, to reach your boxes Waystone a Waystones waystone. The first time someone activates it, it gets a generated name; with Routes installed, it takes the settlement's name Nurse Joy stands behind the counter between the healing machines. She can't be hurt, never despawns and has nothing to trade: she is there for the look Champions Trainer with Champions Training installed, a trainer stands beside the counter. Talk to it to change your Pokémon's stat points, nature, ability and moves Loot the Center's chests, barrels and pots hold Poké Balls, apricorns, food and medicine

The Center sells nothing.

docs.title: The Poké Mart
docs.text:
The Poké Mart sells everyday supplies for CobbleDollars. Prices are in CobbleDollars; Poké Ball prices match CobbleDollars' own default shop.

No clerk yet

In this build the Mart's building stands in every Town, but no clerk stands behind its counter, so its shop cannot be opened from the Mart yet.

Poké BallsMedicineBattle Items Item Price Poké Ball 2,000 Citrine, Verdant, Azure, Roseate and Slate Ball 2,000 each Premier Ball 2,000 Great Ball 6,000 Ultra Ball 8,000 Item Price Potion 2,000 Super Potion 7,000 Antidote 2,000 Paralyze Heal 3,000 Burn Heal 3,000 Ice Heal 1,000 Awakening 1,000 Item Price X Attack, X Defense, X Sp. Atk, X Sp. Def, X Speed, X Accuracy 10,000 each Dire Hit 10,000 Guard Spec. 15,000

Stronger medicine and held items are left to specialised shops.

A datapack can replace the whole shop by overriding its id, cobblemon_poketowns:poke_mart (see For Pack Authors).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
PokeTowns has no config file and no commands. There are two settings, both chosen when the world is created.

Setting Where Default Replace vanilla villages the data pack screen when creating a world on Settlement spacing the PokeTowns tab when creating a world 34 chunks Minimum gap the PokeTowns tab when creating a world 8 chunks

docs.title: Vanilla villages
docs.text:
While the built-in data pack PokeTowns: Replace Vanilla Villages is on, vanilla villages stop generating and PokeTowns settlements take their place. It is on in every new world.

To keep vanilla villages alongside PokeTowns, open Data Packs on the create-world screen and move PokeTowns: Replace Vanilla Villages to the Available side.

While the pack is on:

  • only the vanilla village set is emptied; villages that other mods add in their own sets still generate;
  • pillager outposts no longer keep their distance from villages, because there are no vanilla villages for them to avoid.

On a dedicated server

A server has no create-world screen. To start a server world without the pack, list the data packs with /datapack list on a test world, then add the pack's id to initial-disabled-packs in server.properties before the world is first generated. Turning the pack off in a world that already exists only affects chunks generated afterwards.

docs.title: Settlement spacing
docs.text:
The PokeTowns tab sits next to Game, World and More on the create-world screen.

Slider Range Default What it does Settlement Spacing 10–80 chunks 34 the world is cut into squares this many chunks wide, and each square may hold one settlement. Lower spacing means more settlements Minimum Gap 1 to one less than the spacing 8 two settlements never start closer than this. It always stays below the spacing, and moving the spacing down pulls it down with it

The defaults are vanilla villages' own. The values are saved with the world and never change after it is created. /locate and Routes use the world's own values.

Defaults apply when

A dedicated server, a world created without opening the tab, and a world that existed before PokeTowns was installed all use 34 and 8.

docs.title: Community Credits
docs.text: PokeTowns stands on other people's work. Thank you! 💚

docs.title: Builds
docs.text:
• Cobblemon Additions (CC0): the houses, streets, lamp posts, Pokémon Center, Poké Mart and the gym Towns' battle pad are its builds, used as stand-ins until PokeTowns' own replace them.
  • COBBLEVERSE: the Kanto gyms and their leaders in gym Towns. PokeTowns reads them from the COBBLEVERSE datapack when it is installed and ships none of them.
  • Minecraft: the farms are vanilla's.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: PokeTowns targets Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric and NeoForge.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Version Notes Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric Loader or NeoForge 0.17.3+ / 21.1+ Waystones needs Fabric Loader 0.17.3 or newer Fabric API any Fabric only Fabric Language Kotlin or Kotlin for Forge any / 5.10+ the one for your loader Architectury API any both loaders Cobblemon 1.8.0 or newer Cobblemon 1.7.x is not supported CobbleDollars any the Poké Mart sells through it Waystones any every Pokémon Center holds a waystone. Waystones brings Balm as its own requirement

Optional: Routes connects PokeTowns settlements to its road network. COBBLEVERSE's datapack gives gym Towns their Kanto gym leaders (see Gyms).

PokeTowns does not bundle any of these. If one is missing, the game refuses to start and names it.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Cobblemon, CobbleDollars and Waystones, with their own requirements.
  2. Drop the PokeTowns jar for your loader into mods/. Never put both loaders' jars in.
  3. On a server, install it on the server and on every player's game.
  4. Create a new world. The PokeTowns tab on the create-world screen sets how far apart settlements are (see Configuration).
  5. Find a settlement with /locate structure #minecraft:village, or explore.

New world recommended

Settlements only appear in chunks generated after PokeTowns is installed. In an existing world they show up only in land you have not explored yet, and the settlement spacing of an existing world is always the default (34 and 8 chunks).

docs.title: Gyms
docs.text: Three Towns in ten are gym Towns: a gym stands behind the Pokémon Center, reached by a path from the Center's back yard. Otherwise a gym Town grows like any other Town.

docs.title: With COBBLEVERSE
docs.text:
When the COBBLEVERSE datapack is installed, the gym is one of its seven land gyms, with its leader inside: Brock, Lt. Surge, Erika, Koga, Sabrina, Blaine or Giovanni.

Each gym Town picks one of the seven at random. PokeTowns reads the gym from the datapack and ships none of it, so the building, the leader and the battle are COBBLEVERSE's.

docs.title: Without COBBLEVERSE
docs.text: A battle pad from Cobblemon Additions stands where the gym would be.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Two gym Towns can end up with the same leader; nothing yet hands each leader out only once.
  • PokeTowns needs Cobblemon 1.8 or newer. If your copy of the COBBLEVERSE modpack still runs Cobblemon 1.7, PokeTowns will not start in it.

docs.title: For Pack Authors
docs.text: PokeTowns' settlements are data: structures, template pools, tags and a shop, all in the cobblemon_poketowns namespace. This page lists the ids other datapacks and mods can rely on.

docs.title: Structures and tags
docs.text: Id Kind What it is cobblemon_poketowns:village structure the Village cobblemon_poketowns:town structure the Town without a gym cobblemon_poketowns:town_gym structure the gym Town cobblemon_poketowns:settlements structure set all three, at weights 60, 21 and 9 #minecraft:village structure tag PokeTowns adds its three structures, so anything that looks for villages finds them #cobblemon_poketowns:has_gym structure tag every settlement with a gym; today town_gym #cobblemon_poketowns:has_structure/settlement biome tag where settlements may start. It pulls in vanilla's five has_structure/village_* tags; add a biome here to let settlements spawn in it

docs.title: Placement
docs.text: The settlements set uses the placement type cobblemon_poketowns:world_spread. It is vanilla's random_spread in every way (/locate, explorer maps and Routes treat it as one), except that its spacing and separation come from the world, as chosen on the PokeTowns tab, and not from the JSON. A datapack that overrides the set keeps the per-world values as long as it keeps this placement type.

docs.title: Gyms
docs.text:
• Every gym piece's template id starts with cobblemon_poketowns:gym/. A mod can tell it is inside a gym by that prefix.
  • Gym Towns pick from the pool cobblemon_poketowns:town/gyms. When none of its gyms can be placed, the pool falls back to cobblemon_poketowns:town/gym_fallback, the battle pad.

docs.title: Docking another pack's building
docs.text:
cobblemon_poketowns:docked is a template pool element that places a building from another datapack without copying it. It is how the COBBLEVERSE gyms get into gym Towns.

{
  "element_type": "cobblemon_poketowns:docked",
  "location": "cobblemon_poketowns:gym/cobbleverse/brock",
  "building": "cobbleverse:brock",
  "processors": "minecraft:empty",
  "projection": "rigid"
}
Field Meaning location the anchor: a template the building's size that holds the jigsaw that docks it and the path out of its door building the other pack's template, read by id. It is placed first, at the same origin and rotation as the anchor processors, projection as in a vanilla single_pool_element

If the building template is not installed, the element offers no jigsaw, so generation moves on to the next element and then to the pool's fallback. A missing building is never an error.

docs.title: The Poké Mart's shop
docs.text: The Mart's stock is a CobbleDollars datapack shop with the id cobblemon_poketowns:poke_mart, at data/cobblemon_poketowns/cobbledollars/shop/poke_mart.json. A datapack that ships a file at the same path replaces the whole shop.

docs.title: Vanilla villages
docs.text: The built-in pack PokeTowns: Replace Vanilla Villages overrides only minecraft:villages, the vanilla village structure set, and leaves it empty. Villages that other mods add in their own sets keep generating. See Configuration to turn it off.

docs.title: Settlements
docs.text:
PokeTowns adds three kinds of settlement. Each one grows from a plaza with a Pokémon Center, and the bigger ones add a Poké Mart and a gym.

Settlement Share of settlements In the plaza Size Village about 2 in 3 Pokémon Center streets reach up to 80 blocks from the plaza Town about 1 in 4 Pokémon Center and Poké Mart, facing each other two to three times the streets and houses of a Village, up to 96 blocks out Gym Town about 1 in 10 a Town's plaza, plus a gym behind the Center like a Town

docs.title: Where they appear
docs.text:
Settlements appear in the biomes vanilla villages use: plains and meadows, desert, savanna, snowy plains and taiga. They are placed on a world-wide grid, about as often as vanilla villages by default; the Configuration page shows how to change that.

The ground under each piece is smoothed as the settlement generates, so buildings sit on the land rather than float over it.

docs.title: What is inside
docs.text:
Streets. A crossing at the plaza sends two or three cobbled streets out, and they keep branching. Lamp posts stand along a Village's streets. A Town's streets leave the plaza both north and south.

Houses and farms. Each street has a house on one side and a farm on the other. The houses have kitchens, bedrooms, attics and workshops, with loot to find in their chests. The farms are vanilla's.

Villagers. Vanilla villagers live in the houses, and you trade with them as in any village.

The plaza. The Pokémon Center is always there; in a Town the Poké Mart faces it across the square.

docs.title: Finding them
docs.text:
All three count as villages, so anything that looks for villages finds them, Routes included.

Command Finds /locate structure #minecraft:village the nearest village of any kind, PokeTowns' included /locate structure cobblemon_poketowns:village the nearest PokeTowns Village /locate structure cobblemon_poketowns:town the nearest Town without a gym /locate structure cobblemon_poketowns:town_gym the nearest gym Town /locate structure #cobblemon_poketowns:has_gym the nearest settlement with a gym

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• On steep ground, streets follow the slope while buildings stay level, so a settlement on a hillside can end up with buildings at very different heights.
  • The houses, streets, Pokémon Center and Poké Mart are stand-ins from Cobblemon Additions (see Community Credits) until PokeTowns' own buildings replace them.
